description: Loop runner hardening against the usage-limit failure mode (R1–R7). Make the loop distinguish environmental death (pause/sleep/halt) from a genuinely blocked work item, reconcile committed-but-unrecorded work, add a circuit breaker, right-size the iteration budget, and ship first-class reset/resume. Source incident and rationale: plans/review-agent-feedback-on-playful-kahan.md.

items.title: Extract execGit into a shared git-exec module
items.description:
Move the private execGit function out of packages/loop/src/git-commit.ts into a new packages/loop/src/git-exec.ts, exported as `execGit(cwd: string, args: string[]): Promise<string>`.

Preserve exact behavior: on error, reject with an Error whose message is stderr||stdout||error.message and which carries `stdout` and `stderr` string properties (isNothingToCommit depends on them). Update git-commit.ts to import execGit from ./git-exec.js and delete its local copy. Do not change git-commit's public API, the commit message format, or RUNTIME_EXCLUDE_PATHSPECS. This is a pure extraction with no new behavior.
acceptanceCriteria: packages/loop/src/git-exec.ts exists and exports execGit(cwd, args)
The error path still attaches stdout and stderr properties to the thrown Error

Existing git-commit behavior and tests are unchanged
Verify passes: pnpm test && pnpm typecheck && pnpm lint && pnpm build && pnpm format:check
items.notes: Prerequisite for git-reconcile (002) and the reset/resume commands, which all shell out to git. Keep the function body byte-for-byte identical during the move.

items.title: Add git-reconcile helper: findItemCommit and isTreeClean
items.description:
Create packages/loop/src/git-reconcile.ts with two functions that use execGit from ./git-exec.js and return core Result types (never throw on git failure):

1. findItemCommit(projectPath, itemId): Promise<Result<{ commitHash: string } | null>> — runs `git log --extended-regexp --grep='^\[rauf\] <id>:' --format=%H -n 1` and returns the first matching commit hash, or null when none. Anchor with `^\[rauf\] ` and the trailing colon so id 003 does not match 030 or 0030.
2. isTreeClean(projectPath): Promise<Result<boolean>> — runs `git status --porcelain` and returns true when output is empty.

Export both from the package barrel (src/index.ts). Add packages/loop/src/git-reconcile.test.ts that builds a temp git repo (init, set user, make commits with `[rauf] 001: ...` messages) and asserts: a matching id returns its hash, a missing id returns null, no prefix-matching, isTreeClean true on a clean tree and false after an uncommitted change.
acceptanceCriteria: findItemCommit returns the commit hash for a committed [rauf] <id>: item and null when absent
findItemCommit anchors the match so id 003 does not match 030 or 0030
isTreeClean returns true on a clean tree and false with uncommitted changes
Both functions return Result and never throw on git failure
git-reconcile.test.ts covers all the above against a temp repo
Verify passes: pnpm test && pnpm typecheck && pnpm lint && pnpm build && pnpm format:check
items.notes: Reuse execGit (item 001). These helpers back in-loop commit reconciliation (009) and the reset/resume commands (011/012).

items.title: Add exit-classifier module with classifyExit and hasUsageLimitInText
items.description:
Create packages/loop/src/exit-classifier.ts — a pure, side-effect-free classifier for a finished claude spawn.

1. Move USAGE_LIMIT_PATTERNS out of runner.ts into this module and export `hasUsageLimitInText(text: string): boolean` (case-insensitive substring match).
2. Export `type ExitClass = 'done' | 'blocked' | 'needs_human' | 'usage_limited' | 'timeout' | 'infra_error' | 'genuine_retry'`.
3. Export `const INFRA_FAST_MS = 10_000`.
4. Export classifyExit(result, signal: ParsedSignal): ExitClass where result has { exitCode, stdout, stderr, reconstructedText?, timedOut, durationMs }:
   - explicit signal done/blocked/needs_human → that class
   - else if hasUsageLimitInText(reconstructedText||stdout) OR hasUsageLimitInText(stderr) → usage_limited
   - else if timedOut → timeout
   - else if exitCode !== 0 && durationMs < INFRA_FAST_MS → infra_error
   - else → genuine_retry

Add exit-classifier.test.ts covering every branch, including the incident banner "You've hit your session limit · resets 5:30pm" present ONLY in reconstructedText (must be usage_limited, not genuine_retry).
acceptanceCriteria: classifyExit returns each ExitClass for the documented inputs
Banner present only in reconstructedText classifies as usage_limited
Fast (<INFRA_FAST_MS) code!=0 exit with no banner classifies as infra_error
timedOut classifies as timeout; clean/long no-signal classifies as genuine_retry
hasUsageLimitInText and INFRA_FAST_MS are exported; tests cover all branches
Verify passes: pnpm test && pnpm typecheck && pnpm lint && pnpm build && pnpm format:check
items.notes: Do NOT wire this into the runner here — that is item 006. Keep the module free of side effects and of imports beyond the ParsedSignal type (exported from ./signal-parser.js) so it stays trivially unit-testable.

items.title: Add deferred-vs-blocked distinction and paused_usage_limit to schemas
items.description:
Let the runner record items the RUNTIME gave up on, distinct from items the agent explicitly blocked. In packages/core/src/schemas.ts:

1. BacklogItemSchema: add optional `deferred: z.boolean().optional()` (mirrors needsHuman). Do NOT add a status enum value — deferred items keep status 'blocked' plus this flag.
2. LoopStateSchema: add `deferredItems: z.array(z.string())` (writers default to []; missing parses as []).
3. LoopStateStatusSchema: add 'paused_usage_limit' (clean-halt status used by item 007).
4. packages/core/src/status.ts: update writeLoopState to accept/persist deferredItems; update mapLoopStateStatus and parseDoneFileState to handle paused_usage_limit (map to a PAUSED-like derived state).
5. packages/core/src/backlog.ts: in updateItem, clear the deferred flag when an item transitions to done or pending (as it already clears needsHuman on done).

Keep backward compatibility: existing state.json without deferredItems must still parse.
acceptanceCriteria: BacklogItem accepts an optional deferred boolean; deferred items keep status 'blocked'
LoopState has deferredItems and writeLoopState persists it

Verify passes: pnpm test && pnpm typecheck && pnpm lint && pnpm build && pnpm format:check
items.notes: Foundational for runner wiring (006), reset (011), and status (013). Avoid a new status enum value for the item itself — a boolean flag keeps VALID_STATUS_TRANSITIONS untouched.

items.title: Detect usage-limit banner in claude stdout/stream, not just stderr
items.description:
Current behavior: the runner checks only stderr for usage-limit banners (hasUsageLimitInStderr, runner.ts ~575 and ~915), but the session-limit banner arrives in the reconstructed stdout stream. A fast usage-limit death therefore falls through to signal 'none' and is wrongly retried then blocked. This single blind spot caused all 24 false blocks in the source incident.

Fix: in runIteration (packages/loop/src/runner.ts), after computing signalText (reconstructedText||stdout, ~591), change the pre-signal usage check to call hasUsageLimitInText (from item 003) on BOTH stderr AND signalText. Keep the existing routing: on detection, reset the item to pending and call handleStderrUsageLimit (sleep-or-exit). Remove the now-redundant private hasUsageLimitInStderr/USAGE_LIMIT_PATTERNS in favor of the shared helper.

Add test-sandbox/scenarios/usage-limit-stdout.sh: a mock claude that prints the session-limit banner to stream-json stdout and exits code=1 within ~1s. Add an assertion in test-sandbox/verify.sh that the item stays pending (NOT blocked) and the loop pauses/sleeps.
acceptanceCriteria: The pre-signal usage check scans signalText as well as stderr
A fast code=1 exit with the banner only in the stream is treated as usage-limited; the item stays pending, not blocked
Private hasUsageLimitInStderr is replaced by the shared hasUsageLimitInText

bash test-sandbox/verify.sh passes
Verify passes: pnpm test && pnpm typecheck && pnpm lint && pnpm build && pnpm format:check
items.notes: Load-bearing fix: alone it prevents the 24 false blocks (incident reconstructed banner len=64). Here only EXTEND the existing pre-signal usage check; the full none-case dispatch rewrite is item 006.

items.title: Route no-signal exits through exit-classifier; never block on a missing signal
items.description:
Replace the `case 'review': case 'none':` retry-then-block block in runIteration (packages/loop/src/runner.ts ~672-704) with a dispatch on classifyExit(claudeResult.value, parsed) from item 003. A missing signal must NEVER, by itself, mark an item blocked.

Mapping:
- usage_limited → reset item to pending, route to handleStderrUsageLimit; return its continue/exit (belt-and-suspenders with item 005).
- timeout → item-specific real attempt: mark blocked with reason 'Timed out after <n>s'.
- infra_error → reset item to pending; increment a consecutiveInfraFailures counter (consumed by the breaker in item 008); do NOT block; continue.
- genuine_retry → keep the existing retry-up-to-maxRetries; on exhaustion set status 'blocked' with deferred: true and reason 'No signal after N attempts (deferred by runner)', push to a new deferredItemIds array, write state with deferredItems.

Track deferredItemIds alongside completedItemIds/blockedItemIds (~89-91) and include it in writeState (deferredItems) and buildSummary.
acceptanceCriteria: No code path marks an item blocked solely because parseSignal returned none
usage_limited routes to the usage handler; timeout blocks with a timeout reason
infra_error leaves the item pending and increments the infra-failure counter
genuine_retry exhaustion sets status blocked + deferred:true and tracks it in deferredItems
writeState and buildSummary include deferredItems; existing sandbox scenarios still pass
Verify passes: pnpm test && pnpm typecheck && pnpm lint && pnpm build && pnpm format:check
items.notes: Depends on the deferred schema (004) and classifier (003). Just MAINTAIN the consecutiveInfraFailures counter here; the breaker that acts on it is item 008.

items.title: Stop burning iterations on no-op deaths; parse banner reset time; add paused_usage_limit halt
items.description:
Three budget/usage refinements in packages/loop/src/runner.ts:

1. Iterations should count attempts, not API rejections. iterationCount is incremented at runIteration start (~378). When an iteration ends as usage_limited or infra_error with no work done, decrement iterationCount (or guard the increment) so these no-ops do not drain the budget; appendLog a note when an iteration is not counted.
2. In handleStderrUsageLimit (~987-1006), when the OAuth token is unavailable, parse the reset time from the banner with /resets\s+(\d{1,2}(?::\d{2})?\s*[ap]m)/i and sleep until that local time plus a small buffer instead of the flat 60s; fall back to 60s if no match.
3. Add a sleepOnLimit option (default true) to LoopRunner options. When false, on a 5h usage limit write state 'paused_usage_limit' (item 004), write a DONE summary with a one-line resume hint (e.g. 'paused_usage_limit:<resetsAt> — run `rauf resume`'), and exit cleanly instead of sleeping.
acceptanceCriteria: usage_limited/infra_error no-op iterations do not consume the iteration budget and are logged
Missing-token usage handling parses the banner reset time and sleeps to it (60s fallback)
sleepOnLimit=false halts with status paused_usage_limit and a resume hint in DONE
sleepOnLimit defaults true (unattended sleep behavior unchanged)
Verify passes: pnpm test && pnpm typecheck && pnpm lint && pnpm build && pnpm format:check
items.notes: Reset-time parsing only applies when the API token is unavailable (the OAuth path already returns resetsAt). The paused_usage_limit DONE summary is consumed by `rauf resume` (item 012).

items.title: Add a circuit breaker for consecutive infra failures
items.description:
Stop the loop from grinding through the whole budget when every spawn dies the same way. In packages/loop/src/runner.ts, use the consecutiveInfraFailures counter from item 006 (incremented on each infra_error, reset to 0 on any done/blocked/needs_human/real attempt). Add a circuitBreakerThreshold option (default 3). When consecutiveInfraFailures >= threshold, halt the loop: write state 'error' with a clear message ('Circuit breaker: N consecutive infra failures — halting'), emit the appropriate loop_error/loop_completed events, write a DONE summary, release the lock, and stop spawning. Log the threshold in the run-header at startup.

Add test-sandbox/scenarios/fast-infra-death.sh (repeated fast code=1, no banner) and assert in verify.sh that the breaker halts before maxIterations.
acceptanceCriteria: consecutiveInfraFailures resets on any real outcome and only infra_error increments it
Reaching circuitBreakerThreshold (default 3) halts the loop with a clear error status and DONE summary instead of continuing to maxIterations
The threshold is configurable and logged in the run header
test-sandbox/scenarios/fast-infra-death.sh added and asserted; bash test-sandbox/verify.sh passes
Verify passes: pnpm test && pnpm typecheck && pnpm lint && pnpm build && pnpm format:check
items.notes: usage_limited deaths are handled by the usage path (sleep/halt) and must NOT count toward the infra breaker — only no-banner infra_error exits increment it.

items.title: Reconcile committed work before recording a non-done outcome
items.description:
An iteration can pass verify and commit `[rauf] <id>:` but die before printing RAUF_DONE (the incident's item 003, committed yet marked blocked). Before the runner records any non-done outcome for the current item (blocked/deferred/infra/timeout paths in runIteration), call findItemCommit(projectPath, item.id) and isTreeClean(projectPath) from item 002.

- If a matching commit exists AND the tree is clean → record the item done (updateItem status done), push to completedItemIds, emit item_completed, appendLog 'recovered_via_commit: <hash>', and do NOT call gitCommit again. Skip the would-be block/defer.
- If the tree is dirty after a failed iteration → appendLog and revert to a clean base (git reset --hard via execGit, or stash with a note) before the next iteration so the next item never starts on a half-finished tree.

Add test-sandbox/scenarios/commit-no-signal.sh: a mock claude that commits a `[rauf] <id>:` change then exits with no signal; assert the item ends done (recovered_via_commit), not blocked.
acceptanceCriteria: When a [rauf] <id>: commit landed and the tree is clean, the item is recorded done (recovered_via_commit) rather than blocked/deferred
A dirty tree after a failed iteration is reverted/stashed before the next item
gitCommit is not double-invoked on recovery
The reconciliation check runs for ALL non-done exit classes before the block/defer is written
test-sandbox/scenarios/commit-no-signal.sh added and asserted; bash test-sandbox/verify.sh passes
Verify passes: pnpm test && pnpm typecheck && pnpm lint && pnpm build && pnpm format:check
items.notes: Use git-reconcile (002) and execGit (001). This single check would have correctly recorded the incident's item 003 as done.

items.title: Right-size maxIterations from the backlog and surface the math
items.description:
Replace the flat DEFAULT_MAX_ITERATIONS=20 default with a backlog-derived estimate when --iterations is not given.

1. Add computeMaxIterations(backlog, opts?: { safety?: number; retryHeadroom?: number }): { cap, pending, avgIters, needed } to packages/core/src (new budget.ts, exported from the barrel). cap = ceil(pending * avgEstimatedIterations * safety) + retryHeadroom; safety default 1.5, retryHeadroom a small constant; avgEstimatedIterations from items' estimatedIterations (default 1); pending counts status 'pending'. Keep 20 as a floor when there are pending items.
2. In packages/cli/src/loop-commands.ts (loop run and loop start), when --iterations is omitted, use cap and log: '<pending> pending × ~<avg> iter = ~<needed> needed; cap <cap> (<x>× headroom)'.
3. Mirror the default in packages/web/src/server/routes/loop.ts.
4. Unit-test computeMaxIterations (empty backlog, mixed estimatedIterations, all-pending).
acceptanceCriteria: computeMaxIterations returns the documented cap and inputs and floors at 20 when pending items exist
loop run/start use it when --iterations is omitted and log the budget math
An explicit --iterations still overrides the computed cap
The web loop route uses the same default
Unit tests cover empty/mixed/all-pending backlogs
Verify passes: pnpm test && pnpm typecheck && pnpm lint && pnpm build && pnpm format:check
items.notes: Combined with item 007 (no-op iterations don't count), this keeps the budget meaningful for long backlogs that straddle a usage reset.

items.title: Add `rauf reset` command with commit reconciliation and false-block requeue
items.description:
Add a top-level `rauf reset [--keep-done]` command (register in packages/cli/src/commands.ts; new handler packages/cli/src/reset-commands.ts) so recovery is one command, not manual JSON edits. Steps, in order:
1. Refuse if the loop lock PID is alive (reuse checkLock / staleness from packages/core/src/lock.ts); proceed only when the lock is stale/absent, and clear a stale lock.
2. Commit reconciliation: for each non-done item, if findItemCommit + isTreeClean (item 002) show a landed clean commit, mark it done.
3. Requeue FALSE blocks: items with deferred:true → back to pending (clear deferred/blockedReason). Items with an explicit agent block (status blocked, not deferred, not needsHuman) stay blocked and are reported.
4. resetStalledItems (in_progress → pending), clear state.json/blockedItems, remove .rauf/DONE.
Print a summary (recovered, requeued, kept-blocked, lock cleared). Build on existing resetProject/unblockItems where possible; --keep-done leaves done items as-is (the default).
acceptanceCriteria: rauf reset refuses when a live loop holds the lock and clears a stale lock
Committed-clean non-done items are promoted to done
deferred false-blocks return to pending while genuine agent blocks stay blocked and are reported
state.json/blockedItems and .rauf/DONE are cleared; a summary is printed
rauf backlog validate . still passes after a reset
Verify passes: pnpm test && pnpm typecheck && pnpm lint && pnpm build && pnpm format:check
items.notes: Distinguish genuine blocks via the deferred flag (004): deferred=requeue, plain blocked (agent said RAUF_BLOCKED)=keep. Reuse git-reconcile (002) and core lock/reset helpers.

items.title: Add `rauf resume` command to continue an interrupted loop
items.description:
Add a top-level `rauf resume` command (commands.ts + handler) that detects an interrupted run and continues it:
1. Read derived status / state.json. Recognize resumable states: paused_usage_limit, limit_reached, error (circuit breaker), or a dead lock with non-done items.
2. Apply the same reconciliation + false-block requeue as `rauf reset` — extract a shared helper rather than duplicating the logic.
3. Continue from the first non-done item by launching the loop via the normal entrypoint (same path as `rauf loop run`/`loop start`), honoring --backlog and a recomputed budget (item 010).
If the lock PID is alive, refuse with a message that a loop is already running.
acceptanceCriteria: rauf resume detects paused_usage_limit/limit_reached/error/dead-lock states
It applies commit reconciliation and requeues false blocks before relaunching
It refuses when a live loop holds the lock
It continues from the first non-done item using the normal loop entrypoint
Verify passes: pnpm test && pnpm typecheck && pnpm lint && pnpm build && pnpm format:check
items.notes: Resume = reconcile + requeue-false-blocks + relaunch. Share the reconciliation/requeue helper with item 011 to avoid drift.

items.title: Enrich `rauf status` with lock liveness and blocked/deferred breakdown
items.description:
Extend `rauf status` output (packages/cli/src/status-commands.ts) to make a usage-limit aftermath legible. Add:
1. A lock line: whether .rauf/.loop.lock exists and whether its PID is alive (reuse checkLock from packages/core/src/lock.ts) — e.g. 'Lock: PID 1234 (alive)', 'stale', or 'none'.
2. The last signal from state.json (lastSignal).
3. A backlog breakdown splitting blocked into genuine blocked (explicit agent block / needsHuman) vs deferred (deferred:true, runner gave up), using item-flag counts.
Keep the existing exit-code mapping; add the new lines to both human and --json output.

items.title: Deploy runtime .gitignore entries into target projects on install
items.description: New rauf installs can leave runtime files (.rauf/.loop.lock, state.json, DONE, CANCEL, iteration-status.json, rauf.log, backlog.json.bak) trackable in the target repo — the source incident committed .loop.lock. git-commit already excludes them per-commit, but the target's .gitignore should also cover them. items.title: Document exit taxonomy, reconciliation, budget, and reset/resume

- docs/SPEC-CORE.md: the exit taxonomy (done/blocked/needs_human/usage_limited/infra_error/timeout/genuine_retry), the 'never block on a missing signal' rule, commit reconciliation (recovered_via_commit), the circuit breaker, and computeMaxIterations.

items.title: Fix exit-classifier reconstructedText empty-string fallback
items.description:
In packages/loop/src/exit-classifier.ts (~line 64), classifyExit computes `const signalText = result.reconstructedText ?? result.stdout`. The `??` operator only falls back on null/undefined, so an empty-string reconstructedText ("") skips the stdout usage-banner scan — inconsistent with the runner, which uses a length-check. A usage banner present only in stdout (with an empty reconstructedText) would then misclassify as genuine_retry.

Fix: change to `const signalText = result.reconstructedText && result.reconstructedText.length > 0 ? result.reconstructedText : result.stdout;`. Add a test in packages/loop/src/exit-classifier.test.ts: a no-signal result with reconstructedText:"" and stdout containing the incident banner classifies as 'usage_limited' (not 'genuine_retry').
acceptanceCriteria: classifyExit uses a length-based fallback (not ??) for reconstructedText -> stdout

exit-classifier.test.ts covers the empty-reconstructedText case
Verify passes: pnpm test && pnpm typecheck && pnpm lint && pnpm build && pnpm format:check

items.title: Escape itemId in findItemCommit grep pattern
items.description:
packages/loop/src/git-reconcile.ts (~line 25) interpolates itemId raw into an extended-regex grep: `--grep=^\[rauf\] ${itemId}:`. Backlog IDs are usually numeric but the schema allows any non-empty string, so an ID containing ERE metacharacters could overmatch or error.

Fix: escape the itemId's ERE metacharacters (. ^ $ * + ? ( ) [ ] { } | \) before interpolation, keeping the existing `^\[rauf\] ` anchor and trailing colon. Add a test in git-reconcile.test.ts: an itemId like "1.0" must NOT match a commit message `[rauf] 1x0:` (the dot is treated literally).
acceptanceCriteria: itemId ERE metacharacters are escaped before being embedded in the grep pattern
The anchor and trailing colon are preserved (003 still does not match 030)
git-reconcile.test.ts covers a metacharacter id not overmatching
Verify passes: pnpm test && pnpm typecheck && pnpm lint && pnpm build && pnpm format:check
items.notes: From Codex review (LOW). Prereq for 018, which extends findItemCommit's signature. Keep the helper returning Result and never throwing.

items.title: Bound commit reconciliation to the run baseline (no stale-commit recovery)
items.description:
findItemCommit greps ALL git history, so on a clean tree any item whose ID ever had a `[rauf] <id>:` commit is falsely promoted to done. This is critical because rauf restarts IDs at 001 for every new backlog — an old `[rauf] 001:` from a prior cycle would falsely recover a fresh item 001 during reset/resume or in-loop reconciliation.

1. Schema: add `baseCommitHash: z.string().nullable()` (optional, default null) to LoopStateSchema in packages/core/src/schemas.ts; writeLoopState persists it; old state.json without it still parses.
2. git-reconcile.ts: add an optional `sinceRef?: string` param to findItemCommit; when provided, scope the search with a `<sinceRef>..HEAD` range so only commits after the baseline match.
3. runner.ts: at loop start capture current HEAD (execGit rev-parse HEAD) as baseCommitHash, persist it in state, and pass it as sinceRef to the in-loop reconciliation (~line 992).
4. packages/cli/src/recovery.ts (reset/resume): read baseCommitHash from state and pass it as sinceRef; when state has no baseCommitHash, do NOT auto-promote genuine `blocked` (non-deferred) items, to avoid false recovery.
5. Tests: a clean repo with an old `[rauf] 001:` commit and a current pending/blocked 001 must NOT be recovered when sinceRef excludes it; a commit after the baseline IS recovered.
acceptanceCriteria: LoopState carries an optional baseCommitHash; old state.json without it still parses
findItemCommit accepts an optional sinceRef and scopes the search to <sinceRef>..HEAD
The runner records baseCommitHash at loop start and the in-loop reconciliation uses it
reset/resume recovery uses baseCommitHash and does not promote stale historical commits
Tests cover stale-commit-no-recovery and post-baseline recovery
Verify passes: pnpm test && pnpm typecheck && pnpm lint && pnpm build && pnpm format:check

items.title: Narrow dirty-tree cleanup to the rauf backlog path, not all backlog.json

packages/loop/src/runner.ts (~line 1048) dirty-tree cleanup excludes every `**/backlog.json` in the repo, so a failed item that left an application file literally named backlog.json dirty would have that change swept into the next item's commit.

Fix: restrict the exclusion to the resolved rauf backlog path (paths.backlog) and its `.bak` sibling, plus the `.rauf/**` runtime files — all relative to projectPath — instead of a repo-wide `**/backlog.json` glob. Behavior for the actual rauf backlog/runtime files must stay identical. Add a regression test asserting an unrelated dirty file named backlog.json elsewhere in the tree is NOT preserved by the cleanup.

items.title: Hold the loop lock across reset/resume recovery (close TOCTOU race)
items.description:
packages/cli/src/reset-commands.ts (~49) and resume-commands.ts (~137) guard with guardLoopLock() (check) then mutate backlog/state in recoverInterruptedLoop() — a check-then-mutate TOCTOU race lets a concurrent `rauf loop run` acquire the lock and start between the check and the mutation.

Fix: acquire the loop lock (core acquireLock from packages/core/src/lock.ts) for the recovery window, refuse with a clear LOCK_CONFLICT message if a live lock exists, and release it in a finally block before any relaunch. Use owner-aware release so recovery never deletes a lock owned by a live different PID. Reuse acquireLock/releaseLock/checkLock — do not reimplement PID checks. For resume, hand off cleanly: release the recovery lock before launching the loop via the normal entrypoint (which acquires its own lock).
acceptanceCriteria: reset/resume acquire the loop lock before mutating state and release it in finally
A live lock held by another alive PID makes reset/resume refuse with LOCK_CONFLICT and perform no mutation
Recovery never deletes a lock owned by a live different PID
A test simulates a live lock and asserts reset/resume refuse without mutating
Verify passes: pnpm test && pnpm typecheck && pnpm lint && pnpm build && pnpm format:check
items.notes: From Codex review (HIGH). Land after 018 (both edit recovery.ts). Reuse core lock staleness; resume must release before relaunch so the loop's own lock acquisition succeeds.

items.title: Make server stop/restart loop-aware (refuse with in-flight loops)
items.description:
The shared server daemon (one process on 127.0.0.1:5173 across all projects) has a SIGTERM handler in packages/web/src/server/start.ts (~118) that calls manager.shutdownAll(), cancelling EVERY project's in-flight loop — so unrelated server ops kill your loop. Per-project keying already exists (packages/web/src/server/loop-manager.ts resolveKey/stopLoop). Make destructive ops deliberate:
1. Add LoopManager.listActive(): { projectPath: string }[] and a GET /api/loops route (packages/web/src/server/routes/loop.ts) returning the in-flight loops.
2. In packages/cli/src/server-commands.ts handleServerStop/handleServerRestart: before SIGTERM, fetch /api/loops; if any loop is in-flight, REFUSE (non-zero exit) and list the affected projects unless --force is passed.
3. Verify ensureServerRunning (packages/cli/src/loop-commands.ts ~104) never restarts a healthy server; add a test asserting it no-ops when the server is healthy.
4. On rauf loop start, print a one-line notice that a server stop/restart will interrupt this loop and that `rauf loop run` is the unattended-safe mode.
Do NOT try to re-adopt a killed loop's claude child (it dies with the server) — out of scope.
acceptanceCriteria: rauf server stop and restart refuse (non-zero exit) and list affected projects when any loop is in-flight, unless --force
LoopManager exposes the active-loop list and GET /api/loops returns it
ensureServerRunning does not restart a healthy server (a test asserts it no-ops when healthy)
rauf loop start prints a notice that a server restart interrupts it and names `loop run` as unattended-safe
Verify passes: pnpm test && pnpm typecheck && pnpm lint && pnpm build && pnpm format:check
items.notes: From feedback #2 F1 (critical operational hazard). Per-project keying already exists; only shutdownAll ignores it. Re-adoption of the child is explicitly out of scope. Files: server-commands.ts, loop-manager.ts, routes/loop.ts, loop-commands.ts.

items.title: Recover verified-but-uncommitted work on resume (re-verify + commit)
items.description:
A kill in the verify->commit window leaves verified work UNCOMMITTED with no `[rauf] <id>:` commit; commit-reconciliation (item 009) only recovers when a commit exists. Today packages/cli/src/recovery.ts reconcileAndRequeue (~103-132) skips reconciliation when the tree is dirty, and reset/resume/loop run either refuse or stash it.
1. recovery.ts: when the tree is DIRTY and an item is in_progress with NO commit at/after baseCommitHash, classify it as an interrupted iteration and report it distinctly: 'item <id> left uncommitted changes (interrupted before commit)' — not the generic dirty-tree refusal.
2. rauf resume (resume-commands.ts) gains --recover: re-run the project's verify command (resolved from the .rauf.json/RAUF.md profile via packages/core/src/profile.ts) for the interrupted item; on green, commit the changes as `[rauf] <id>: <title>` and mark the item done; on failure, leave the work untouched and report. Default (no --recover) only surfaces, never mutates.
3. git-status.ts: the dirty-tree refusal message points to `rauf resume --recover`.
acceptanceCriteria: A dirty tree with an in_progress item and no baseline commit is reported as an interrupted iteration, not a generic dirty-tree refusal
rauf resume --recover re-runs verify and, on green, commits the work as [rauf] <id>: and marks the item done
On failed re-verify the work is left untouched and the failure is reported
The dirty-tree refusal message points to rauf resume --recover
Tests cover interrupted-iteration detection and re-verify-then-commit (mocked passing verify)
Verify passes: pnpm test && pnpm typecheck && pnpm lint && pnpm build && pnpm format:check
items.notes: From feedback #2 F2 (high). Complements item 009 (commit-exists recovery). Reuse baseCommitHash (018) + findItemCommit; the verify command comes from the profile. Files: recovery.ts, resume-commands.ts, reset-commands.ts, git-status.ts.

items.title: Intercept --help/-h before side effects + per-subcommand flag help
items.description:
Current incorrect behavior: `rauf loop start --help` STARTS the loop — packages/cli/src/main.ts only intercepts --version/-V before dispatch, so --help falls through to handleLoopStart. Also `rauf help loop start` only lists subcommand names; the per-subcommand `usage` (defined in commands.ts) is never rendered and there is no flag-level help.
Fix:
1. In main.ts (and/or parser.ts): detect --help/-h in the parsed flags BEFORE invoking any command/subcommand handler, and route to help output — before any side-effecting action.
2. In packages/cli/src/commands.ts showCommandHelp: when help targets a command+subcommand, render the subcommand `usage` plus a flag list. Add a flags description (name + meaning) to the loop run/start subcommand defs and render it.
3. Unknown flags on side-effecting commands surface help rather than silently starting work.
acceptanceCriteria: rauf loop start --help (and -h) prints help and does NOT start the loop or daemon
rauf loop run --help prints the flag list (--iterations/--retries/--timeout/--model/--backlog/--force/--create-branch/--ndjson/etc.) and does not run
rauf help loop start renders the subcommand usage + flags, not just the subcommand list
--help is intercepted before any handler side effect; a test asserts loop start --help exits without starting a loop
Verify passes: pnpm test && pnpm typecheck && pnpm lint && pnpm build && pnpm format:check
items.notes: From feedback #2 F5 (a help probe mutated state). Files: main.ts, parser.ts, commands.ts.

items.title: Resolve maxIterations by precedence and log the source
items.description:
maxIterations resolution is confusing: the CLI computes a default from the backlog (item 010) when --iterations is omitted but IGNORES `.rauf.json` options.maxIterations. Establish one logged precedence in packages/cli/src/loop-commands.ts (loop run + loop start), mirrored in packages/web/src/server/routes/loop.ts:
1. Resolve as: explicit --iterations flag > `.rauf.json` options.maxIterations (read via packages/core/src/profile.ts readMarkerFile) > computeMaxIterations(backlog).
2. Log the resolved value AND its source at startup: `maxIterations=<n> (flag|.rauf.json|computed)`.
3. Keep the computeMaxIterations budget-math line (item 010) only when the source is `computed`.
Do NOT change the runner's options plumbing — only where the value is resolved before LoopRunner.create / the API request body.
acceptanceCriteria: maxIterations precedence is flag > .rauf.json options.maxIterations > computed-from-backlog
Startup logs the resolved value and its source (flag / .rauf.json / computed)
The web loop route applies the same precedence
A unit test covers all three precedence sources
Verify passes: pnpm test && pnpm typecheck && pnpm lint && pnpm build && pnpm format:check

items.title: Derive status RUNNING vs PAUSED from liveness, not staleness
items.description:
Current incorrect behavior: packages/core/src/status.ts deriveFromStateJson (~114-149) downgrades running->PAUSED when state.json updatedAt is older than ~5 min (STALENESS_THRESHOLD_MS). state.json is only written between iterations, so a long (15-30 min) active iteration is mislabeled PAUSED. Expected: an actively-working loop shows RUNNING.
Fix: before the running->PAUSED staleness downgrade, consult liveness signals:
1. Lock-PID liveness via packages/core/src/lock.ts checkLock — if the lock PID is alive, keep RUNNING.
2. iteration-status.json freshness via packages/core/src/iteration-status.ts readIterationStatus — if its updatedAt/mtime is recent, keep RUNNING (it is written ~every 5s with token counts during an iteration).
Only downgrade to PAUSED when the lock PID is dead OR no fresh iteration-status exists. Keep current behavior for genuinely dead/stale loops. Do not spawn subprocesses (status derivation reads files only).
acceptanceCriteria: A long active iteration (stale state.json updatedAt but live lock PID and fresh iteration-status.json) reports RUNNING, not PAUSED
A genuinely dead loop (dead lock PID, stale iteration-status) still reports PAUSED
deriveStatus consults checkLock and readIterationStatus before the staleness downgrade and spawns no subprocesses
Tests cover live-PID+fresh-iteration-status -> RUNNING and dead-PID+stale -> PAUSED
Verify passes: pnpm test && pnpm typecheck && pnpm lint && pnpm build && pnpm format:check
items.notes: From feedback #2 F7. Item 013 added lock liveness to the DISPLAY only, not the derivation. Reuse checkLock + readIterationStatus. Files: status.ts.

items.title: Add `rauf loop run --create-branch` + actionable refuse message
items.description:
packages/loop/src/git-status.ts checkLoopPreconditions refuses on the default branch / dirty tree with only generic advice, so reaching a runnable state is manual. In packages/cli/src/loop-commands.ts handleLoopRun (mirror in handleLoopStart):
1. Parse --create-branch <name> (extractStringFlag). When set and not already on that branch, switch via execGit(projectPath, ['switch','-c',name]) (packages/loop/src/git-exec.ts) BEFORE checkLoopPreconditions; fail cleanly if the branch exists or the switch errors.
2. When checkLoopPreconditions refuses, print exact copy-pasteable remediation: the `git switch -c <branch>` command, the `--seed-backlog` step (item 028), and the `--force` escape — replacing the generic 'commit or stash' line.
Keep --force behavior intact.

items.title: Add `rauf loop run --ndjson` machine-readable event stream
items.description: Direct-mode `rauf loop run` emits only human-rendered output plus a final --json summary; supervising it programmatically means hand-rolling a tail|grep on rauf.log. Add a --ndjson flag to handleLoopRun (packages/cli/src/loop-commands.ts): when set, the runner event subscription emits one JSON object per line to stdout (JSON.stringify(event) + '\n') for every LoopEvent, and SUPPRESSES the formatted renderer (formatAndPrintEvent) and the StatusLine so stdout is a clean NDJSON stream. The final result still prints as a trailing JSON line. --ndjson forces no-color and disables the status line. Reuse the existing event subscription (~723-788) and the LoopEvent union (packages/core/src/schemas.ts).
acceptanceCriteria: rauf loop run . --ndjson emits exactly one valid JSON object per line, one per LoopEvent, to stdout

items.title: Add `rauf loop run --seed-backlog` to auto-commit the backlog
items.description: backlog.json is git-tracked (correctly — its status changes are meaningful), so an uncommitted freshly-authored backlog gets swept into item 001's commit when the loop marks the first item in_progress. Do NOT add backlog.json to RUNTIME_EXCLUDE_PATHSPECS (would break progress tracking).

items.description:
